title: tearrubr
tagline: Make it possible to verify a physical product without having to trust the seller.
description:
TearRubr is a product authentication platform that gives physical products a verifiable digital identity.

Manufacturers register products with TearRubr and associate each product with a unique identifier. When a customer purchases an item, they can scan its TearRubr code and verify whether the product corresponds to a legitimate record.

The goal is simple:

Make it possible to verify a physical product without having to trust the seller.

TearRubr uses blockchain as a public, tamper-resistant verification layer while keeping application data and user-facing functionality in conventional infrastructure.
how_its_made:
TearRubr is built as an end-to-end physical product authentication platform that bridges industrial manufacturing lines with the Ethereum blockchain.

Architecture & Tech Stack:

Smart Contracts & Blockchain: We authored and compiled the TearRubr.sol registry contract in Solidity using Hardhat and deployed it live to the Ethereum Sepolia testnet (0xa34C7D37BB2bf41f73e562075878E86eFc7Ed05B). Transactions are signed and broadcast server-side using Ethers.js v6 connected via Alchemy's Sepolia RPC API.
Frontend & UX: Built with SvelteKit (leveraging Svelte 5 runes for reactive state) and custom Tailwind CSS.
Backend & Storage: SvelteKit server endpoints handle on-chain transactions, supply-chain verification APIs, and persist local metadata with Drizzle ORM and SQLite (better-sqlite3).
Notable Technical Solution (The Scalability Problem): High-volume FMCG goods (like Coca-Cola bottles) cannot afford an individual on-chain transaction for millions of units. To solve this, we engineered an industrial Batch Merkle Rollup engine:

The factory inputs batch parameters, and the system generates thousands of unique serialized product twins ([PREFIX]-[BATCH]-[INDEX]).
We compute a deterministic Merkle Tree Root across all serial hashes.
Only the single 32-byte Merkle root is committed on-chain in one transaction, making high-throughput production cost-effective.
The platform exports a factory-ready CSV print manifest directly compatible with industrial packaging laser coders (Videojet/Domino).
auto_summary: A SvelteKit application and Solidity registry for registering and verifying physical products using Sepolia, SQLite, Privy authentication, and a custom The Graph subgraph.
